interpretation_profile.target_resolution: local bom-ref; external BOM-Link recorded but not followed
interpretation_profile.scope_reference_entries: objects with an own string-valued ref property
interpretation_profile.scope_reference_closure: one hop from expression/target seeds; newly resolved nodes are not scanned
interpretation_profile.containment: RFC 9535 normalized-path equality or descendant-token boundary
interpretation_profile.refs_restriction: reference-value path must be inside the current node-set subtrees
interpretation_profile.referrers_holder: object owning the property, or object owning one containing array; nested arrays are outside this bounded profile
interpretation_profile.scoped_referrers: replace the current set with matching referring objects; do not retain input nodes, per #1067 head d3fca0c prose
interpretation_profile.whole_document_referrers: identity whenever the current node set contains the document root, including omitted scopes, an explicit $ scope, and a preceding identity step
interpretation_profile.duplicate_bom_ref: diagnostic; ambiguous reference is not resolved
interpretation_profile.dependencies: unsupported in the bounded P0 probe and rejected fail-closed
interpretation_profile.required_completeness: not decided by this evaluator; #1067 head d3fca0c states any-match per scope, one scope per subject for a per-subject verdict, and consumer policy for empty-value sufficiency

decision_points: The prose defines one completeness evaluation per scope but not the required/recommended pass/fail aggregation rule within that scope.
The scope prose names object entries with a ref property; raw string references are traversed only when a mapping via expression selects them.
A scope containing several seed subjects does not define whether completeness is collective or per subject.
Empty selected values have a path match but no defined completeness meaning.
